items.title: Three arrested after raid on gang accused of helping migrants pretend to be gay to get asylum
items.summary: Those targeted by Home Office immigration enforcement officers are accused of charging migrants up to £4,500 for fabricated evidence.

items.title: Watch: Police raid on gang behind fake gay asylum claims
items.summary: The arrests come after a BBC investigation in April revealed that law firms and advisers were helping migrants pose as gay in an effort to get asylum.

items.title: US death row inmate Christa Pike awake and speaking after failed execution, lawyers say
items.summary: Experts and lawyers called the apparent recovery unprecedented, noting she is believed to be the only known person to survive a lethal injection.

items.title: Tear gas in Paris and Marseille as school protests grow across France
items.summary: Crowds of mainly teenagers called for more resources for schools and an end to what they called police repression.

items.title: I'd rather have another election than do a deal with Reform UK, says Badenoch
items.summary: The Conservative Party leader also pledged to cut the cost of hiring 21 to 24 year olds.

items.title: Green member behind Zionism motion named as 'close friend' of jailed al-Qaeda supporter in court
items.summary: Lubna Speitan offered to testify on behalf of Minh Quang Pham, who was jailed for 40 years after a Heathrow bomb plot investigation.

items.title: What can I do to protect myself after 'Asos hacked' message?
items.summary: Asos says people should not engage with the unauthorised notification and says it'll provide further information.

items.title: UK risks being 'uninvestable' if new oil and gas fields not approved, warns Equinor
items.summary: Equinor warns it may shun further investments in the UK if new oil and gas fields at Rosebank and Jackdaw are not approved.
